verses.text: After this, Absalom got himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run ahead of him.

He would get up early and stand beside the road that led to the city gate. Whenever someone came with a case for the king to judge, Absalom would call out to him, "Which town are you from?" The man would answer, "I am from one of the tribes of Israel."
Then Absalom would say, "Look, your case is good and right, but the king has no one to listen to you."
Absalom would also say, "I wish I were made judge in this land! Then anyone with a case or complaint could come to me, and I would make sure he was treated fairly."
And whenever someone came near to bow down to him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.
Absalom did this to all the Israelites who came to the king for judgment. In this way he stole the hearts of the people of Israel.
After forty years, Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go to Hebron to keep a promise I made to the LORD.
While I, your servant, was living in Geshur in Syria, I made this promise: 'If the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD.'"
The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he got up and went to Hebron.
But Absalom sent secret messengers through all the tribes of Israel to say, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, shout, 'Absalom is king in Hebron!'"
Two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom. They had been invited as guests, and they went innocently, knowing nothing about the plan.
While Absalom was offering sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel from Giloh, who was David's adviser, to come from his town of Giloh. So the plot grew stronger, and more and more people joined Absalom.
A messenger came to David and said, "The hearts of the people of Israel have gone over to Absalom."

Then David said to all his officials who were with him in Jerusalem, "Get up! We must run away, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry, or he will quickly catch up with us, bring disaster on us, and kill the people of the city with the sword."
The king's officials answered him, "Your servants are ready to do whatever our lord the king decides."
So the king left, with his whole household following him. But he left ten of his slave wives behind to take care of the palace.
The king went out with all the people following him, and they stopped at the last house.
All his officials marched past him, along with all the Kerethites and Pelethites, the king's guards. All six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath also marched past the king.
The king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why are you coming with us? Go back and stay with the new king. You are a foreigner, an exile from your own land. Go back to your own place.

You only came yesterday. Should I make you wander around with us today, when I don't even know where I am going? Go back, and take your brothers with you. May the LORD show you his faithful love and truth."
But Ittai answered the king, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as surely as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king is, whether it means life or death, there your servant will be."
David said to Ittai, "Go ahead and march on." So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and all the children who were with him.
All the people of the land cried loudly as all the people passed by. The king crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people went on toward the wilderness.
Zadok was there too, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of God's covenant. They set down God's ark, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had finished leaving the city.
Then the king said to Zadok, "Take God's ark back into the city. If the LORD is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see the ark and the place where it stays again.
But if he says, 'I am not pleased with you,' then here I am. Let him do to me whatever he thinks is best."
The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Aren't you a seer, someone who sees what God is doing? Go back to the city in peace, with your son Ahimaaz and Abiathar's son Jonathan.
I will wait at the river crossings in the wilderness until I get a message from you telling me what is happening."
So Zadok and Abiathar took God's ark back to Jerusalem and stayed there.
David went up the Mount of Olives, crying as he went. His head was covered and he walked barefoot. All the people with him also covered their heads and cried as they went up.
Someone told David, "Ahithophel is one of those plotting with Absalom." So David prayed, "LORD, please make Ahithophel's advice foolish."
When David reached the top of the hill, where people worshipped God, Hushai the Arkite came to meet him. His coat was torn and he had dust on his head.
David said to him, "If you come with me, you will only be a burden to me.
But if you go back to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, my king. I used to serve your father, but now I will serve you,' then you can help me by spoiling Ahithophel's advice.
The priests Zadok and Abiathar will be there with you. Tell them everything you hear in the king's palace.
Their two sons are there with them: Ahimaaz son of Zadok, and Jonathan son of Abiathar. Send them to me with everything you hear."
So David's friend Hushai arrived in the city just as Absalom was coming into Jerusalem.
